The transcription tool I use on my Mac, MacWhisper, has rolled out another major update today, adding real-time meeting transcription, significantly improved speaker diarization, deeper Apple Intelligence integration, and an all-new transcription model. Here are the full details.

MacWhisper's deeper Apple Intelligence integration

I've previously written about how I rely on MacWhisper, especially in my podcast production workflow.

MacWhisper was one of the first AI-powered transcription tools for Mac. Since launching in 2023 from indie developer Jordi Bruin, it has continued to evolve and expand its support for new models, services, and workflows.

That includes automatic meeting recording, speaker diarization, watch folders, system-wide dictation, local and cloud-based AI models, and integrations with services like Notion, Zapier, Obsidian, and n8n.

Today MacWhisper has been upgraded to version 15.2, which adds an improved speaker diarization feature powered by the NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Diarization model that was announced just hours ago.

Which brings us to the other big feature in this update: real-time meeting transcription.

The feature, which has sat near the top of MacWhisper's public roadmap, is finally rolling out now and lets users review, reference, copy, or send live transcripts while a meeting is still in progress.

As for actual transcription models, MacWhisper 15.2 adds Alibaba's QWEN3-ASR transcription model, which supports 22 languages, along with tighter integration with Apple Intelligence, Siri, Spotlight, and Shortcuts in macOS 27.

Now, users on macOS — including those in the European Union — can search transcriptions system-wide, open them with Siri, drag text into Shortcuts, and reference the on-screen transcript within Siri or Apple Intelligence requests.

Finally, MacWhisper 15.2 adds folders and subfolders for organising transcripts and meeting notes, and supports dragging existing transcripts into them from the sidebar.
